name: allProps
signature: allProps(obj: any, opt: string = 'tvp', depth = 6): GenObj | [] | string | boolean

description.brief: Inspects an object to return as many properties as possible, with optional values, types, or both, and optional filtering.
description.detailed: This function performs a deep inspection of an object's properties, including inherited properties. It allows for retrieving property keys only, or keys with values, types, or both.  It also allows for filtering out common built-in properties for cleaner results. The depth parameter controls the recursion level for nested objects. If the object is not parsable (primitive, null, or specific built-in objects), it returns the type of the object. The function uses recursion to handle nested objects up to a specified depth. If an exception occurs during property access, an error object is returned for that property.

params.name: opt
params.description: A string specifying what information to return. 't' includes the type, 'v' includes the value, 'p' includes the parsed value (recursive call for nested objects), and 'f' includes all properties without filtering.  Defaults to 'tvp'.

params.name: depth
params.description: The maximum recursion depth for nested objects. Defaults to 6.

relatedFunctions.name: getProps
relatedFunctions.description: Used to retrieve property names from the prototype chain.

relatedFunctions.name: filterProps
relatedFunctions.description: Used to filter out built-in properties.

relatedFunctions.name: typeOf
relatedFunctions.description: Used to determine the type of a value.

relatedFunctions.name: isBuiltIn
relatedFunctions.description: Used to check if a value is a built-in object.

exampleUsages.description: Get all properties with values and types:
code: const myObject = { a: 1, b: 'hello', c: { d: true } };

exampleUsages.description: Get parsed properties with a limited depth:
code: const myObject = { a: 1, b: { c: 2, d: { e: 3 } } };

exampleUsages.description: Get all properties including built-in properties

sourceCode:
/**
 * Inspect an object to get as many props as possible,
 * optionally with values, types, or both - optionally filterd
 * by props
 * @param obj - what to test
 * // @param depth number - what to return
 * //0: just array of prop keys
 * //1: object of keys=>value
 * //2: object of keys => {type, value}
 * @param string opt any or all of: v|t|p|f 
 * If 'v' - the raw value
 * If 'p' - a parsed, readable value
 * If 't' - the value type

 * If none of t,v, or p  just array of props

 * If at least one of t,v,p, abject {prop:{value,type,parsed}

 * If f - FULL property details. Default: filter out uninteresting props
 * 
 * @param int depth - how many levels should it go?
 */
export function allProps(obj: any, opt: string = 'tvp', depth = 6): GenObj | [] | string | boolean { 
// ... function body ...
}
parameterInterdependencies: The `opt` parameter influences the structure and content of the returned object. The `depth` parameter affects how deeply nested objects are parsed when 'p' is included in `opt`.

errors.description: An exception can occur if there's an error accessing a property. In this case, an error object with details is returned for the specific property.

return.description: If `obj` is not an object, returns the type of `obj` as a string. If `obj` is a primitive or certain built-in objects, returns an object with the value, type, and parsed value. Otherwise, if none of 't', 'v', or 'p' are in `opt`, returns an array of property keys. If any of 't', 'v', or 'p' are in `opt`, returns an object where keys are property names and values are objects containing the value, type, and/or parsed value as specified by `opt`. If an error occurs during property access, the value for that property will be an error object. If the recursion depth is exceeded, returns the string 'END'.

notes: The function uses a set of predefined properties to keep (keepProps) and built-in properties to filter out (builtInProps).

edgeCases.description: Accessing properties with getters that throw errors.
example: const myObject = { get a() { throw new Error('Getter error'); } };
edgeCases.consequence: The returned object will contain an error object for the property with the getter error.
The function will recurse until the depth limit is reached, returning 'END' for the deeply nested objects.
